activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Related Rates With Circles and Spheres

feedback.problem: The radius of a circle is increasing. At a particular moment, the rate of increase of the area of the circle is numerically equal to three-fifths of the rate of increase of the diameter. Determine the radius of the circle at that moment.
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $r$  be the radius, $A$ the area, and $D$ the diameter of the circle. We wish to find $r$ at the moment when $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=\frac{3}{5}\frac{\text{d}D}{\text{d}t}.$

To start, let's set up an equation relating the area $A$ and the diameter $D$ of the circle. Since $D=2r$ and $A=\pi {r}^{2},$ the relationship between $A$ and $D$ is

$$
A=\pi {r}^{2}=\pi {(\frac{D}{2})}^{2}=\frac{\pi {D}^{2}}{4}.
$$

Differentiating this relationship with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\pi {D}^{2}}{4}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}D}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}D}(\frac{\pi {D}^{2}}{4}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}D}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\pi D}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=\frac{3}{5}\frac{\text{d}D}{\text{d}t},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5}\frac{\text{d}D}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}D}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\pi D}{2} \\ \frac{3}{5} & =\frac{\pi D}{2} \\ D & =\frac{6}{5\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, since $D=2r,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2r & =\frac{6}{5\pi } \\ r & =\frac{3}{5\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
